parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the church letters sit around the one

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone claims an archbishop could run the church single-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Runcie was Archbishop of Canterbury 1980-91. 'Without' means outside here, so CE goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Runcie held the see of Canterbury, the subject named at 14.

clue.text: Into which, by analogy, a gallon won't go

definitions.text: Into which, by analogy, a gallon won't go

parts.words: Into which, by analogy, a gallon won't go
parts.note: echoes the saying that you cannot put a quart into a pint pot, scaled up one size of measure

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel holding a quarter of a gallon cannot take the full gallon, as the proverb about pint pots suggests.

clue.text: Suppress mounting attacks on the French

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means the word rises, read from bottom to top

parts.note: fits are sudden attacks of illness or temper
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone holds down a rising wave of assaults on France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' turns FITS upside down in the grid to give STIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle a yawn or protest is to suppress it.

definitions.meaning: to ... a task is to begin it
the alimentary canal, a zoologist's word for the gut

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a phrasal verb for starting; read as one it is the anatomical name for the gut.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An archbishop goes fishing while thinking about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Fisher was Archbishop of Canterbury 1945-61 and crowned Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Fisher was one of the holders of the see at 14.

definitions.meaning: Randall ... held the see at 14 from 1903 to 1928
King Solomon was the son of King David, so cryptically a David's son; the question mark flags the wordplay

explanation.definitionFit: Randall Davidson was a holder of the see at 14, and Solomon was literally the son of David.

clue.text: 14 with a month for holidays (one on Tyneside?)

parts.note: August is the classic summer holiday month
the Roman numeral for one is I
Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: An archbishop takes a summer break, perhaps somewhere around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustine was the first Archbishop of Canterbury, sent in 597. 'On' just puts I beside NE; Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: St Augustine founded the see at 14 and was its first holder.

clue.text: Soldier climbs back into vehicle for a smoke

indicators.note: says the soldier's letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: climbing back means the soldier's word is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier gets back in the truck for a cigarette break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbs back' reverses the soldier; in an across clue 'climbs' is only a reversal cue, nothing vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is something rolled for smoking, so it is a smoke.

clue.text: One breaking the surface is more alarming, if included

indicators.note: says the little word goes inside the comparative

parts.note: scarier means more alarming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thing that cracks the surface is more frightening, if you count it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One breaking the surface' sounds like a diver or whale; it is a tool for loosening soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarifier is a tool that breaks up soil or road surfaces, or makes scratches in the skin.

clue.text: President may be found here daily about one

indicators.note: says the cleaner's word goes round the one

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning woman, also called a char
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A president can be found here every day, give or take one.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or CHAR is a British cleaner who comes in each day, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever presides at a meeting occupies the chair, so that is where a president sits.

indicators.note: keep just the first half of the word for a tongue

parts.note: a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: An archbishop speaks only half of a language.
explanation.walkthrough: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42; half of LANGUAGE is LANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmo Gordon Lang was one of the holders of the see at 14.

definitions.meaning: William ..., and his father Frederick, both held the see at 14
a building dedicated to worship, such as a Jewish or Hindu shrine

explanation.definitionFit: Two archbishops bore this surname, and the common noun means a house of worship.

clue.text: A sorter's sorted, being a woman of her word

indicators.note: things sorted are rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the possessive here counts as a letter, giving the word with an S

explanation.surface: A clerk who sorts papers is a woman who keeps her promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted' rearranges A SORTERS, with the S of the 's counted.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratress is a female orator, a woman whose trade is words.

clue.text: He gives leads to church and nation, though ultimate authority's royal

indicators.note: the leading letters of each of the following words are taken

parts.words: church and nation, though ultimate authority's royal

explanation.surface: The archbishop guides church and country, yet the final say lies with the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The archbishop signs as Cantuar, short for the Latin for Canterbury. 'Leads to' takes the first letter of every word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantuar is the signature of the Archbishop of Canterbury, so he is the man meant.

clue.text: A religious heretic involved with making honey

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or religious
an Arian followed Arius, whose views on Christ were condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A pious heretic takes up beekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is old slang short for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiarian describes anything to do with beekeeping, which produces honey.

clue.text: A mother for a motherless man

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: A woman takes on the mothering of a man who never had one.
explanation.walkthrough: The first man was made, not born, so he had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was created from dust, so he alone had no mother.

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for divorce

explanation.surface: Someone gives an excuse for being left high and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run aground is stuck on the bottom, stranded.

clue.text: English apricot crumble can be overdone

indicators.note: to crumble is to break into pieces, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: An English apricot crumble risks being cooked too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumble' looks like the pudding but rearranges E and APRICOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic behaviour is melodramatic and exaggerated, theatrical to excess.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here giving the letter A
a scribe was a copyist or writer of old

explanation.surface: A trait belonging to an ancient author.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something to someone is to attribute it to them.

clue.text: 14 discovering God's name for himself in testaments

indicators.note: the divine name sits inside the testaments

parts.note: a will is a last testament
God tells Moses his name is I AM in Exodus

explanation.surface: An archbishop finds the name of God within the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowan Williams was Archbishop of Canterbury 2002-12. 'Testaments' suggests the Bible but means WILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowan Williams was the holder of the see at 14 when this was set.

clue.text: Ten — nil rout gets the bird

indicators.note: a rout is a disorderly defeat, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ten-nil thrashing earns the losing side a jeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' sounds like being booed, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A linnet is a small brown finch, a songbird.

definitions.meaning: a toast as glasses are raised

explanation.definitionFit: The one British exclamation serves as farewell, drinking toast and thank-you.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from the bottom

parts.note: a nag is a horse
GOC is General Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An archbishop's horse carries a general high up.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Coggan was Archbishop of Canterbury 1974-80. 'Up' turns NAG + GOC into COGGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Coggan was one of the holders of the see at 14.

indicators.note: the shuffled year wraps around the writing
hectic means frantic, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An archbishop has a frantic twelve months full of paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Ramsey was Archbishop of Canterbury 1961-74. 'Hectic' makes RAEY from the year, and 'involving' wraps that round the writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Ramsey was one of the holders of the see at 14.

indicators.note: words broadcast are heard, not seen, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A mayday signal goes out over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress call' looks like one phrase; it splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring someone's heart is to distress them.

parts.note: a pro is a professional, no amateur
a gramme is a very light unit of weight

explanation.surface: Bill is a professional who fights at a low weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre bill lists the show; 'lightweight' is not a boxer here.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre bill or playbill is the printed programme of a show.

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
algebra uses y for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An archbishop frets about what nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: George Carey was Archbishop of Canterbury 1991-2002.
explanation.definitionFit: George Carey was one of the holders of the see at 14.

parts.note: a means one, as in a hundred

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone oddly checks out legal cases about bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' is grammatical: the ablative is a noun case in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablatives are grammatical cases in Latin and other inflected languages.
